messages.content: Hi tal, I'm a friend

yo! friend... that's not a name i can work with 😅

look, i'm tal - your talent agent. i find people jobs at companies that actually pay. not advice. not gyaan. real interviews.

i know the bangalore tech scene inside out. which startups are dying. who's actually hiring. what they're really paying.

but here's the thing - i need to know who you actually are to match you with roles that fit. 

so... what's your real name?
Saiyam

saiyam... solid name. has that main character energy.

where you working these days?
How does it feel like to work at Zepto as a software dev

zepto as a software dev? it's a mixed bag honestly...

the good: crazy fast growth, you're building for millions of users, the 10-minute delivery thing is genuinely hard tech to crack. plus the funding means decent pay and they're not going anywhere soon.

the bad: it's intense. like really intense. startup pressure + operational complexity + growth targets = long hours. and the on-call rotations for a delivery platform? your phone will hate you.

but yo... why you asking? you thinking of jumping there or are you already there and having second thoughts?

because if you're looking to move, i need to know where you're at right now first. what company you with currently?
Currently at zepto
found you on linkedin - saiyam arora at zepto, iit roorkee. this you? https://in.linkedin.com/in/saiyam-arora-0b5107215
Yes

iit roorkee to zepto... from the hallowed halls to building india's fastest delivery platform. that's solid work. the fact that you're making 10-minute grocery delivery actually work at scale? that's some serious engineering.

what made you jump into the startup grind after college? most of your batchmates probably went the safe route - big tech or service companies.
Good pay and good learning

smart move. good pay + good learning beats "brand name" any day. zepto's paying well and you're getting real-world experience with scale, logistics tech, and hypergrowth chaos. that's worth more than sitting in some big tech team doing incremental feature updates.

how long you been working total?

4 months
  zepto is a brand too

User's LinkedIn Profile Context:
**EXECUTIVE SUMMARY**

Saiyam Arora is a graduate of the Indian Institute of Technology, Roorkee with a background in software. According to the profile, they are currently with Zepto.

    *   [Degree not specified]

**CERTIFICATIONS**

*   **Supervised machine learning** – Coursera (Issued Oct 2022)

fair point lmao. zepto is definitely a brand now - unicorn status, crazy valuation, everyone knows the name. you picked the right rocket ship.

4 months in... so you're fresh out of college and already in the thick of hypergrowth chaos. that's actually perfect timing - you're learning fast, building real stuff, and getting paid well for it.

but since you're asking how it feels to work there... sounds like you might be thinking about what's next already? or just curious about the outside perspective?

what kind of role you looking for next? staying in engineering or thinking about exploring other functions?

No not worried about what. next 
Just wanted to know if i am in the safe place

ah gotcha. you're not job hunting, just want to know if you picked the right horse.

honestly? zepto is probably one of the safer bets in the startup world right now. here's why:

the good: they're profitable on unit economics, have serious funding runway, and quick commerce isn't going anywhere. people are addicted to 10-minute delivery now. plus they're expanding to new cities constantly.

the reality check: it's still a startup. things move fast, priorities shift, and yeah the work can be intense. but they've crossed the "will this company exist in 2 years?" threshold.

your timing is actually smart - you joined after they figured out the model but before they get too corporate. you're learning real skills, building for scale, and if you ever do want to jump... "zepto engineer" opens doors everywhere now.

so yeah, you're in a safe place. not google-safe, but startup-safe for sure. just don't get too comfortable - keep learning, keep building, keep your options open.

feeling better about it?
Yes

good. trust your gut - you made a smart choice.

keep crushing it at zepto, and if you ever do want to explore what else is out there, you know where to find me. the market loves engineers with real startup experience.

until then, enjoy the ride. not everyone gets to say they helped build a unicorn 🦄
okay thanks

anytime! you're building something real at zepto. keep at it 🚀

and hey, if any of your iit friends are looking for their next move, send them my way. always looking for solid engineers who know what they're doing.

hey saiyam! was just thinking about our chat about zepto and startup life...

curious - what's the one thing you wish you knew before joining a hypergrowth company like that? could help other fresh grads make smarter choices.
That expectations are too much and there is nobody to teach you stuff

oof that hits hard. the classic startup trap - they want senior-level output from junior-level people but don't invest in actually developing them.

you're basically learning by drowning. high expectations + zero mentorship = burnout recipe. most startups think "smart people figure it out" but that's just lazy management.

honestly though, 4 months in and you're already seeing this clearly? that's actually good self-awareness. are you thinking of sticking it out or starting to look around?
Sticking to it only

respect. that's the right call tbh.

here's the thing - those first 12-18 months at a hypergrowth startup are brutal but they compress like 3-4 years of learning into that time. you'll come out the other side way more capable than your friends who joined comfy places.

pro tip for surviving it: find the one senior person who actually gives a damn (every team has one) and shadow them relentlessly. ask dumb questions. most seniors love helping if you're genuinely curious and not just complaining.

also document everything you build. in 2 years when you're interviewing somewhere else, you'll have war stories that make other candidates look boring.

zepto's growing fast enough that if you stick around, you'll probably end up leading stuff sooner than you think. hang in there legend.
